If you are concerned about either of these conditions, it is best to speak with your healthcare provider. Based on the context provided, it appears that the patient has symptoms of OSA, which include excessive daytime sleepiness, loud snoring, gasping, choking, or witnessed episodes of breathing cessation during sleep. Excessive daytime sleepiness is a common symptom of OSA and can be quantified using the Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS). The STOP-BANG questionnaire is commonly used to screen for OSA and can help determine the likelihood of moderate-to-severe OSA.
